props.title: Corners

B01.capture_spec: C01: scene `final` of evidence/planning-checks/scratch-project/capture_scenes.gd: a MeshInstance2D with a QuadMesh 384 x 168 cut 31 x 7 (297 vertices), cream and teal checker texture of 16 x 7 cells, a grey pole beside the left edge, shader lab-shaders/11-flag-final.gdshader from the first frame; canvas 1280 x 720; record 252 frames (8.4 s: four wave periods at speed 3, so the loop seam is under 1 % of a period out), 30 fps, Forward+, no input.
B01.visual_intent: Act title 'Corners' (serif 40) top-left. A real Godot render in a framed window on the cream stage: a cream and teal checker flag pinned to a grey pole waves smoothly with its folds lit, in a seamless loop. Label: 'live clock'.
B01.motion_claim: The flag is already waving on the first frame: the ripple travels along it while the pole end stays still.
B01.runner_up: manim drawing of a waving flag
B01.why: A real render is the honest picture of what a vertex shader does; a drawing would only claim it.

B02.visual_intent: A rectangle on the cream stage with a terracotta dot on each corner. The dots flash one after another, each with a counter 1, 2, 3, 4 and a small 'where?' tag; then the four dots slide to new places and the rectangle follows as a leaning parallelogram. Caption in the GLOSSARY wording: 'vertex(): runs once for each vertex; places the corners'.
B02.motion_claim: Each corner flashes in turn with its count, then the shape follows the four moved corners.

show.event: dots flash in order, counter 1 to 4

B02.why: The count of four is the claim; four flashes in turn is the count, and the drag shows what the answer does.

B03.visual_intent: A box labelled vertex(). A terracotta dot labelled VERTEX (monospace) arrives from the left at the corner (-64, -64), passes through the box where the line `VERTEX.x += 40.0;` is shown, and leaves on the right at (-24, -64). Caption in the GLOSSARY wording: 'built-in: a value the engine hands to a function'.
B03.motion_claim: The dot goes in, the line acts on it, and a moved dot comes out the other side.

show.event: box and the line of code

B03.why: In and out is a flow; a dot that visibly changes on its way through says it with motion.

B04.visual_intent: A 128 by 128 square with a small cross at its middle and two axis arrows drawn as shapes: x to the right, y pointing DOWN. The four corners get labels in turn: (-64, -64) top left, (64, -64) top right, (-64, 64) bottom left, (64, 64) bottom right; a scale bar '128 px'. Small grey credit: 'measured in Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+'.
B04.motion_claim: Corner labels land one by one; the y arrow points down and the top corners carry the minus sign.

show.event: y arrow pointing down is ringed

B04.runner_up: ShaderLab: Lab render coloured by VERTEX
B04.why: That render needs a varying the film has not taught yet; the drawing, with numbers confirmed by the Lab probes, says it plainly.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Apple M4 Pro · Forward+ · scripted: shader switched on mid-beat

B05.capture_spec: C02: scene `slide` of evidence/planning-checks/scratch-project/capture_scenes.gd (canvas 640 x 360): Sprite2D, checker 128 px at scale 1.0, centred; lab-shaders/01-slide.gdshader assigned at 0.22 of the beat; record from 0 to the event plus 1.5 s and hold the last frame; 30 fps; Forward+. Measured: left edge 256 -> 296.
B05.visual_intent: Code card at left with the one line `VERTEX.x += 40.0;` highlighted; at right a real Godot window (640 by 360): the 128 px checker square sits still, then jumps 40 px to the right as the voice says 'add forty to x' (the shader switches on at 22 % of the beat). A terracotta ring on its new left edge, readout '+40 px'.
B05.motion_claim: The square sits still, then slides forty pixels the moment the shader switches on.

show.event: ring on the new left edge; +40 px

B05.why: A real slide measured to the pixel; a drawing could only illustrate it.

props.videoLabel: Godot 4.7.2 · Apple M4 Pro · Forward+ · scripted: shader switched on mid-beat

B06.capture_spec: C03: scene `local` of evidence/planning-checks/scratch-project/capture_scenes.gd (canvas 640 x 360): two Sprite2D checker squares, scale 1.0 at x 130 and scale 2.0 at x 380; 01-slide on both at 0.52 of the beat; record to the event plus 1.5 s, then hold. Measured: left edge moved 40 px (scale 1.0), 80 px (scale 2.0), 90 px (Lab default scale 2.25).
B06.visual_intent: Same code card. At right, two real Godot squares side by side: one at its own size, one scaled to twice its size, both given the same `VERTEX.x += 40.0` at 52 % of the beat. The small one jumps 40 px, the large one 80 px. Readouts '40 px' and '80 px' under them; label 'same shader'.
B06.motion_claim: Both squares jump at the same instant; the large one travels twice as far.
B06.why: Two real nodes, one shader, two distances: the proof that VERTEX is counted before the node's scale.

B07.capture_spec: C04: scene `squash` of evidence/planning-checks/scratch-project/capture_scenes.gd (canvas 640 x 360): Sprite2D checker 128 px at scale 1.0; 02-squash at 0.35 of the beat; record to the event plus 1.5 s, then hold. Measured box 192 x 64, centre unchanged.
B07.visual_intent: Code card at left with `VERTEX *= vec2(1.5, 0.5);` highlighted; at right a real Godot window: the 128 px square, still, then at 35 % of the beat stretches to 192 px wide and flattens to 64 px tall about its middle. Readout '192×64 px'.
B07.motion_claim: The square stretches wide and flattens about its own middle when the shader switches on.
B07.why: A real squash measured to the pixel (width 192, height 64, centred); a drawing could only illustrate it.

B08.visual_intent: The same square, now with BOTH numberings at each corner in two rows: pixels from the middle (-64, -64) and address (0, 0), then (64, -64)/(1, 0), (-64, 64)/(0, 1), (64, 64)/(1, 1). A terracotta dot visits the corners. Caption in the GLOSSARY wording: 'UV: a point's address on the shape: 0 to 1 across, 0 to 1 down'.
B08.motion_claim: A dot visits the four corners and the address row of numbers lands beside each pixel row.

show.event: top left (0, 0) and bottom right (1, 1) ringed; caption

B08.runner_up: ShaderLab: Lab render coloured by UV
B08.why: Two ways to say where one corner is is a naming claim; both labels on one square show it at a glance.

B09.capture_spec: C05: scene `lean` of evidence/planning-checks/scratch-project/capture_scenes.gd (canvas 640 x 360): Sprite2D checker 128 px at scale 1.0; 03-lean at 0.72 of the beat; record to the event plus 1.5 s, then hold. Measured left edge 256 -> 306 (+50 px over 128 rows).
B09.visual_intent: Code card at left with `VERTEX.x += 50.0 * UV.y;` highlighted; at right a real Godot window: the 128 px checker square, still, then at 72 % of the beat it leans: the bottom edge slides 50 px right while the top stays. A terracotta ring on the bottom edge, readout '+50 px'.
B09.motion_claim: The square shears sideways when the shader switches on: top corners stay, bottom corners go fifty pixels.

show.event: ring on the bottom edge; +50 px

B09.why: A real shear measured to the pixel; the line and its result together are the whole lesson.

B10.visual_intent: The leaning square's left edge drawn as a slanted line with five sample dots along it, labelled with the measured shifts +1, +12, +25, +37 and +49 px (rows 2, 31, 63, 95 and 124 of 128). A caption: 'four corners: straight edges'. Small grey credit: 'Apple M4 Pro · Godot 4.7.2 · Forward+ · straight to within half a pixel'.
B10.motion_claim: The five dots land one after another down the edge, each with its measured number, evenly spaced.

show.event: five dots with numbers, in order

B10.why: The even spacing of five real measurements is the proof that nothing was calculated between the corners.
